report.summary: Chunk 3 of 3: mint.py lines 561-END. Contains _log_mint_diagnostics, mint_task_from_landed_edit, mint_from_commit, confirm_task, load_minted_tasks, save_minted_tasks, add_minted_task, confirm_minted_task. Claims checked.
risks: mint_task_from_landed_edit line 605 | medium | report.get("wrote") may be absent; get returns None, then sorted(... or []) handles it, but if "wrote" is present but not a list, sorted will raise TypeError. | Add explicit type check or ensure caller provides list.

mint_from_commit line 655 | medium | _git result splitlines() assumes newline-separated output; if git output is empty or malformed, iteration may produce unexpected results. | Validate _git return before splitting.

mint_from_commit line 658 | medium | rename case: parts[-1] takes tail path, but if rename has two paths, the first (old path) is ignored; before/after may be incorrect. | Confirm rename handling matches intent.
load_minted_tasks line 678 | low | Uses json.load without try-except; if file exists but is corrupt, raises JSONDecodeError. | Add error handling.
save_minted_tasks line 685 | low | Writes file with 'w' mode; if multiple processes write concurrently, data loss possible. | Use atomic write or lock.
add_minted_task line 694 | low | Overwrites existing task with same id; silent replacement may hide data. | Log overwrites.

handoff.purpose: Implements minting tasks from landed edits and commits, task persistence and confirmation.

symbols.note: Logs skipped and reason from diagnostics dict.

symbols.note: Mints one quarantined task from offload write report.

claims.text: The "reported, never silent" channel for information that doesn't fit the two public mint_* entry points' pre-existing ``dict | None`` / ``list[dict]`` return shape (kept as-is because __main__.py's CLI wiring depends on it). A task that DID mint carries its own ``skipped_out_of_scope``/``must_include_dropped`` fields; this is what surfaces the same information -- and the no-task-minted ``reason`` -- for the cases where there is no task dict to carry it.
claims.why: Function logs skipped and reason from diagnostics dict; it does not return anything and only logs, matching the 'reported, never silent' channel description.

claims.text: ``report`` is (or contains the same "wrote" field as) the dict ``daedalus.offload.offload()`` returns for a write that passed verification. ``report["wrote"]`` IS ``disk_changed`` from offload.py:194-197 -- the files that ACTUALLY changed on disk, found by diffing a before/after content-hash snapshot taken around the run.
claims.why: The claim references offload.py internals not present in this chunk; the code does read report.get('wrote') but does not verify its origin or format beyond sorting.

claims.text: The edit is assumed uncommitted (offload writes straight into the working tree and never commits): "before" is read from git HEAD, "after" from the file currently on disk.
claims.why: Code reads before from _show(repo_root, 'HEAD', rel) and after from _read_worktree(repo_root, rel), consistent with the claim.

claims.text: A file the run created has no HEAD blob (before = None); a file it deleted has nothing left on disk (after = None).
claims.why: Code sets before = _show(...) if sha else None, but _show may return None if file not in HEAD; after = _read_worktree returns None if file missing, matching claim.

claims.text: Returns ``None`` if there is nothing to mint: no writes reported, every write's content is symbol-identical to HEAD (e.g. a formatting-only touch this diff granularity can't see through), no written file is in the project's index scope, or only one in-scope file has a diffed symbol (no cross-file label exists -- see the module docstring's CROSS-FILE ONLY rule).
claims.why: Function returns None if disk_changed empty (line 604), and _mint_from_diffs returns None when no cross-file diff exists; the docstring conditions are handled by _mint_from_diffs.

claims.text: Same idea as ``mint_task_from_landed_edit``, but against history that already exists -- this is what lets minting be exercised deterministically in tests without a live offload run (a temp git fixture IS real git history; ``git show`` gives exact before/after text with no mocking).
claims.why: Function uses _show with explicit sha and parent, consistent with deterministic git history interaction.

claims.text: Currently mints a single aggregate task per commit (via the same ``_mint_from_diffs`` used for landed edits); returns a list so a future split (e.g. one task per hunk, for very large commits) is additive rather than a signature change.
claims.why: Function calls _mint_from_diffs and returns [task] if task else [], matching the single-task-per-commit claim.

claims.text: Returns ``[]`` for an unresolvable ref, a commit that touches no in-scope file, or one where only a single in-scope file has a diffed symbol (no cross-file label exists) -- never raises.
claims.why: Returns [] if full_sha is None (line 646), if name_status is None (line 653), and _mint_from_diffs returns None task leading to [] return (line 669). No exception is raised.
Code increments confirmations (line 675) and sets tier to 'primary' if confirmations >= MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD (line 676-677).

claims.text: A no-op on a task that is not currently quarantined: a primary task doesn't need more confirming, and "confirming" a hand_reachable task is meaningless -- it was never gated in the first place.
claims.why: Function returns early if task.get('tier') != 'quarantine' (line 672), making no changes.

claims.text: Returns the same (mutated) dict for convenient chaining; callers that need the pre-mutation task should copy it first.

This is the ONLY load path by which a minted task can reach ``daedalus.eval.harness.all_tasks()`` and therefore any go/no-go number -- without it, ``mint_task_from_landed_edit``/``mint_from_commit`` produced dicts that lived only as long as the caller's local variable.
claims.why: The claim references daedalus.eval.harness.all_tasks() not present in this chunk; the function only reads the file and returns sorted list.

claims.text: Sorted by id for deterministic iteration (PYTHONHASHSEED-independent), matching the rest of this repo's output-determinism rule.
claims.why: Function returns sorted data with key=lambda t: t['id'] (line 683).

claims.text: Overwrite the mint store with exactly ``tasks``. Deterministic formatting (sorted keys, sorted by id) so the diff is meaningful in review -- same contract as ``harness.write_baseline``.
claims.why: Function sorts tasks by id (line 687), uses json.dump with indent=2, sort_keys=True (line 688), and writes newline (line 689).

claims.text: Persist ``task`` into the mint store, keyed by id. Idempotent: minting the same diff twice (same target + same must_include, via the content hash in ``_mint_from_diffs``) yields the same id and overwrites in place rather than duplicating -- re-running a mint (e.g. after a rebase that reproduces an identical patch) must not inflate the quarantine count.
claims.why: Function loads existing tasks, builds dict by id, inserts/replaces task, and saves; duplicate id overwrites (line 693-695).
Returns result of save_minted_tasks, which returns path (line 695).

claims.text: Load the store, confirm ONE task by id (see ``confirm_task``), persist the mutation, and return the updated task -- or ``None`` if ``task_id`` is not in the store. The only durable way a quarantined mint accumulates confirmations and eventually promotes to primary; ``confirm_task`` alone only mutates an in-memory dict that would otherwise evaporate.
claims.why: Function loads tasks, finds by id, calls confirm_task, saves, returns task; returns None if not found (line 702-707).

observations.what: mint_task_from_landed_edit uses report.get('wrote') which returns None if key missing; sorted(None) would raise TypeError, but the code uses sorted({...} or []) so it's safe.
mint_from_commit uses _git with 'diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-status -r --root' and splits by newline; if output is empty or malformed, iteration may behave unexpectedly.

In mint_from_commit, for a rename, parts[-1] takes the new path; the old path is ignored, but before/after are based on rel (new path). This may be incorrect if the file was renamed and both sides should be considered.
load_minted_tasks uses json.load without exception handling; corrupt file will raise.
save_minted_tasks writes with 'w' mode; concurrent writes may cause data loss.
add_minted_task silently overwrites existing task with same id; if id collision is due to different content, data loss.
